nonBlockingIssues.description: The 'Go to home' link uses a plain <a href='/'> instead of React Router's <Link to='/'>, causing a full page reload instead of client-side SPA navigation. VAL-ROUTE-004 and VAL-CROSS-004 specify client-side navigation. Functionally works but doesn't match contract intent.
nonBlockingIssues.suggestion: Replace <a href='/'> with React Router's <Link to='/'> component.

appliedUpdates.description: Added 'Error Boundary Architecture' section to .factory/library/architecture.md documenting the two-tier pattern, key prop convention, props API, and non-Error handling.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add to CONVENTIONS: 'Error boundaries: All route elements in App.tsx must be wrapped with <ErrorBoundary level="route" key="route-<path>">. The key prop is mandatory for route isolation — without it, React Router reuses the same boundary instance across routes, leaking error state.'
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: Both reviewers flagged this. The key prop requirement was discovered as a bug during visual validation (commit e62bda0) — ErrorBoundary state leaked between routes without unique keys.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add to testing guidance: 'For browser-based error testing, prefer localStorage flags over modifying source code. Set a flag in the component, check it at render time to throw, then clear the flag to test recovery. This avoids git diffs and ensures clean cleanup.'
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: Visual validation worker used localStorage flags successfully to force errors in ThemeProvider and ComponentsShowcase without modifying source files, ensuring clean git state after testing.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Update the frontend-worker skill to recommend React Router's <Link to='/'> instead of plain <a href='/'> for the 'Go to home' navigation in ErrorBoundary's route-level fallback, to align with the validation contract's client-side navigation requirement (VAL-ROUTE-004, VAL-CROSS-004).
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: Both reviewers noted the conflict between skill guidance (recommends <a href='/'> for simplicity) and validation contract (requires client-side navigation). This is a systemic issue that will affect future error boundary implementations if not corrected.
